resources.title: WordPress editor guide
resources.description: Learn blocks, patterns, pages, and posts.

resources.title: Query Loop guide
resources.description: Build article lists and grids that update as you publish.

tips.title: Master a layout you can rebuild
tips.body: Practice one main layout and two variations: a horizontal lead photo, a vertical lead photo, and a text-led arrangement. Rebuild with unfamiliar articles instead of memorizing one finished page.
tips.practice: Rebuild a section from a blank page, then replace the headline with one twice as long.

tips.title: Create a type hierarchy
tips.body: Use consistent styles for section titles, headlines, subheadings, body text, and captions. Start with two font families at most. Judge readability on an actual phone, not just the desktop canvas.
tips.practice: Check whether a reader can distinguish a headline, byline, and caption instantly.

tips.title: Give colors a job
tips.body: Choose a readable background and text combination, plus one primary accent. Use the accent for navigation and section labels. Keep article text high contrast.
tips.practice: Review the page without color: is the hierarchy still clear?

tips.title: Use spacing deliberately
tips.body: Align story edges and keep consistent gaps between cards and sections. Give the lead story more space. Empty space helps separate ideas.
tips.practice: Compare all card padding, image ratios, and section gaps.

tips.title: Let the strongest story lead
tips.body: Select a lead for each section. Give it more visual weight through headline size, placement, and image size. Supporting articles should remain easy to scan.
tips.practice: Ask a teammate which story they notice first.

tips.title: Prepare frameworks, then follow the facts
tips.body: Practice summary, descriptive, anecdotal, and contrast leads. Choose the approach that fits your evidence. Do not force a prewritten argument onto the contest material.
tips.practice: Write two different leads using the same verified reporting.

tips.title: Find an angle with evidence
tips.body: Identify a specific change, conflict, consequence, or human experience. Before drafting, state the angle in one sentence and list the facts and quotes that support it.
tips.practice: Pitch the story in one sentence without using a vague topic label.

tips.title: Distinguish editorial voices
tips.body: News prioritizes verified reporting. An editorial presents the publication’s argued position. A column presents a named writer’s perspective. Features build meaning through reporting and detail.
tips.practice: Check that opinion is clearly labeled and factual claims are supported.

tips.title: Report beyond the final score
tips.body: Collect names, scores, decisive plays, turning points, relevant statistics, and quotes. Sports features explore people; sports editorials argue positions with evidence.
tips.practice: Prepare a game-report checklist before the practice event.

tips.title: Choose photos that report
tips.body: Select informative moments and strong expressions. Crop with purpose without changing the meaning. Add accurate captions and credits; verify names and visible details.
tips.practice: Pick one lead photo and explain what readers learn from it.

tips.title: Make infographics useful
tips.body: Use charts for comparisons, timelines for event order, and fact boxes for key figures. Label units and sources. Keep scales honest and decorative elements secondary.
tips.practice: Explain why the graphic is easier to understand than a paragraph.

tips.title: Design the story preview
tips.body: Use a relevant photo, clear headline, short excerpt, and obvious link to the full story. Avoid repeating the entire article in the section grid.
tips.practice: Open every headline and Read more link on mobile.

tips.title: Everyone learns basic layout
tips.body: Each member should know how to add an article, apply headings, insert photos and captions, assign categories, and preview. One person oversees visual consistency, but does not do every task.
tips.practice: Swap roles during a practice session.

tips.title: Assign clear ownership
tips.body: Give each article or page an owner. Agree on filenames, handoffs, and editing responsibilities. Coordinate before two people edit the same page.
tips.practice: Run one simulation with an agreed handoff sequence.

tips.title: Set internal deadlines
tips.body: Work backward from submission. Set checkpoints for drafts, edited copy, photos, layout, and final review. Leave a real buffer to test access and submit the link.
tips.practice: Record where the team loses time during a full timed simulation.

tips.title: Build sections with categories
tips.body: Organize articles under News, Editorial, Feature, and Sports. Put the sections in the navigation. Individual stories can open on their own pages. Confirm the required structure with organizers.
tips.practice: Publish one sample article per category and test the menu.

tips.title: Use Query Loop for repeated cards
tips.body: Design an article card once, then use Query Loop to show different posts. Filter by category to populate a section automatically. The layout repeats while the content changes.
tips.practice: Publish another Sports post and check whether it appears in the Sports grid.

tips.title: Practice with your actual setup
tips.body: Use the same free plan, theme, and native blocks during training. WordPress.com Free does not support installing additional plugins. Confirm contest-specific tool permissions with organizers.
tips.practice: Rebuild without any paid blocks, plugin dependencies, or imported assets.

tips.title: Read on a phone
tips.body: Check headline wrapping, body size, image cropping, menu behavior, and horizontal overflow. Read a full article instead of only looking at the homepage.
tips.practice: Test a narrow screen and a desktop screen.

tips.title: Verify before you submit
tips.body: Check facts, spelling, names, scores, captions, categories, links, and public access. Remove identifying information as required by contest instructions.
tips.practice: Have a teammate open the published URL without signing in.

tips.title: Train for the contest conditions
tips.body: The supplied guidelines specify five hours for production and submission, cleared laptops, and no identifying marks in the output. They do not explicitly settle plugin permissions, free-plan use, or a four-webpage limit. Confirm regional instructions.
tips.practice: Practice rebuilding from a blank start rather than relying on a saved competition template.
